quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves to the right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
The road winds ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves to the right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right. You should slow down to the speed shown on the sign.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They may drive so poorly that they look drunk.
Opening a window and turning up the radio will keep them alert.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive so poorly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Coffee, open windows, and loud radio are not enough to make a drowsy driver safe.

questions.question: How much lane width are motorcycles allowed to use?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the full width of a lane, just like all other motor vehicles.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
You may see more pedestrians ahead.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: An "End school zone" sign marks where the school zone speed limit ends. You may now drive at the regular speed limit.

questions.question: Is night driving more or less dangerous than day driving?

options.text: Less dangerous.
Just as dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because visibility is worse, headlights can blind you, and tired or impaired drivers are more common at night.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to:

options.text: Vehicles already in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout before entering.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic signals are not working?

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and proceed with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: What should you expect from children playing near the road?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can drive only in the direction it points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: To prepare for anything coming up on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better if you see problems before they happen. Look far ahead of your vehicle, but also check the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes display arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow:

options.text: Is used only on one-way streets.
Means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
Only works if a circular green light is also showing.
Points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can proceed, just like a green light. However, you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at passengers while talking to them while driving.
Only watches the vehicle ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for things in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep checking the road, your mirrors, and your instrument panel regularly. Good habits help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: Turning your head and checking your blind spot before changing lanes, driving away from a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Not needed.
Not needed if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the proper lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Do not make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway ends.
A one-way street begins.
A one-way street ends.
A divided highway begins.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway begins.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead becomes a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

options.text: Yes.
No.
If there is no oncoming traffic.
If the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines down the center mean neither lane can cross, unless turning into a driveway or business. You can cross double yellow lines when turning in or out. You cannot pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: Oregon's Implied Consent Law means that by driving in the state, you agree to:

options.text: Keep liability insurance while you drive.
Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
Post bail or go to court if arrested for a traffic violation.
Keep your vehicle in safe working condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for driving under the influence.
questions.explanation: Oregon's Implied Consent Law means you agree to take a breath, blood, or urine test if a police officer asks. This happens when you are arrested for driving under the influence.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs mean:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you about railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and not try to drive around them.

questions.question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Pull over on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must account for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quieter noise trucks make.
The faster speed trucks travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the road ahead.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Not use your brakes right away.
Slowly slow down and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the bright lights, as this can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: How can you avoid emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe distance lets you react to problems without sudden braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Signal your lane change.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Signal your lane change. Check for other drivers also moving into your lane. Never use your phone while driving.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces this risk.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the lane is clear.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to see the blind spot, and signal every time you change lanes.
